subject: TrueCap #3 — BRRRR math actually works when these 4 things are true
preheader: 30Y -8bp to 6.77% · 3 BRRRR-friendly deals · The refi assumption that kills 80% of plans

marketSnapshot.headline: Rates ticked down, refi window cracking open
marketSnapshot.body: 30Y dropped 8bp to 6.77%, lowest read since February. Bond market is pricing in 2 cuts before EOY — not certain, but the path is there. For BRRRR investors who've been waiting for the refi side of the math to start working again, this is the first real signal in 14 months. Watch the next 3 jobs prints; if any come in soft, expect another 15-25bp leg lower.

dealSpotter.address: Detroit, MI — East English Village SFR
dealSpotter.body: $58k purchase + $32k rehab + $8k holding/financing = $98k all-in. Comparable rehabbed properties trading $140-150k. Rents at $1,300. The post-refi number works only if you can actually get appraisal to $145k+, and Detroit appraisals have been pulling 3-7% under-market in 2025. Build that into the model — assume $135k appraisal, not $145k.

$135k + $48k rehab = $183k all-in, ARV ~$220k. Rents $1,100 each unit = $2,200. At 75% LTV refi ($165k pulled out, $18k locked in), DSCR is only 1.12 at current rates. Works if rates drop another 50bp. Today's rates, you're stuck with capital locked + thin cash flow.

Not a BRRRR — including this because it's a reminder that in some markets, traditional buy-and-hold beats BRRRR friction. $215k for a turn-key 3/2 at $1,825 rent. No rehab, no holding costs, no appraisal risk. Sometimes the boring path is the better path.

blogFeature.title: How to spot a bad rental deal in 60 seconds — 7 red flags
blogFeature.excerpt: The seven red flags every experienced investor checks before opening the full underwrite — rent-to-price ratio, tax-to-value, photo gaps, HOA red zones, age-of-building tells, motivated-seller signals, and rough DSCR at your actual rate.

qa.question: I have $120k saved. Should I do one BRRRR or two traditional buys?
qa.answer: Two traditional buys, usually. One BRRRR consumes most or all of $120k tied up for 6-12 months while you rehab + refi + season, with appraisal risk that can leave you holding $20-40k of trapped capital if comps disappoint. Two traditional buys put $60k each into two cash-flowing properties immediately. The BRRRR math only beats two-buys when you can find a property that pencils at <70% ARV-after-rehab AND you have a contractor track record. If this is deal #1 or #2 for you, traditional is the safer compounding path. Save the BRRRR play for after you've done 3-4 traditional buys.
